# THE STRATEGY LEDGER — what changed, and what happened next

> Operator, 2026-10-06: *"we absolutely need to know why its improving or getting worse? all changes in logic and strategy need to be recorded"* · *"otherwise how do we measure success and failure etc"*

**⚠ REGENERATED BY `scripts/strategy_ledger.py`. Do not hand-edit** — a hand-maintained record drifts from what the code did, and then the account of the experiment becomes the least reliable artefact in it.

## How success is measured, and the one thing this cannot measure

The bar is in `docs/PROJECT_800_A_DAY.md`: **$800/day at 4 lots on the holdout**, with trades/day 3-6, side accuracy ≥0.75 and leg capture ≥0.15. All four, on weeks never trained on and never reviewed.

**The noise floor is $324/day.** That is the measured spread of this harness run twice on IDENTICAL inputs. Any iteration-to-iteration move smaller than it is not evidence of learning, however tidy the story.

**What cannot be measured here:** *which rule* caused a change. Each iteration rewrites up to ten rules at once and is run ONCE. That is correlation. Establishing cause needs the same week re-run with a single rule toggled and everything else held — a separate, more expensive experiment that has not been run. Every "why" below is therefore a DECOMPOSITION of where the money moved, not an attribution.

### What it said it was changing

*No declared CHANGELOG — the requirement was added to `consolidate()` on 2026-10-06 and applies from iteration 4 onward. For earlier iterations the change is RECONSTRUCTED below by `scripts/rule_diff.py`, which is weaker evidence: it is inference from prose, not the author stating intent.*

### What actually changed vs iteration 1 (reconstructed)

```
=== LOGIC CHANGE: iteration 1 → iteration 2 ===
    10 rules → 10 rules

  [DROPPED]
        WAS: Enter on continuation, never on a turn call: with the side long, enter only
        after price makes a new high of the current leg and pulls back without breaking the
        leg's prior low; mirrored for short. If the pullback breaks that low, there is no
        trade — wait for the next new extreme.

  [DROPPED]
        WAS: Expect to enter many times. Target 8–15 entries per session and re-enter the
        same side after every exit, win or lose, as long as rule 4 presents a setup. Four to
        seven trades a day was not selectivity, it was absence: the two worst days of the
        week took 2 and 7 trades, and the flat day took none.

  [DROPPED]
        WAS: A session with no trade is a failure, not a saved loss. If the picture shows
        any leg in progress and you have no position and no entry for over an hour, take the
        next rule-4 setup on the day's side at reduced size rather than keep waiting.

  [DROPPED]
        WAS: Hold each entry until price makes a lower low than the pullback you entered
        from (mirrored for short). Do not exit on a fixed point gain; capturing 1–7% of a
        leg repeatedly is how a losing day is built, and every trade of the week captured
        under half its leg.

  [ADDED]
        NOW: Read the shape before the numbers and classify the day first: if the picture
        shows one or two long swings in the same direction, it is a press day — trade it
        repeatedly at normal size. If it shows four or more swings of similar size with no
        dominant direction, it is chop — minimum size, and after two losers in that state,
        stop for the day. The ten-swing day was the only losing day of the week (−$856); the
        two-swing day was the best (+$940).

  [ADDED]
        NOW: Enter only on continuation: price makes a new extreme in the dominant
        direction, pulls back, and the pullback holds without erasing the prior extreme's
        base. Re-enter on the next such setup after every exit, win or lose. If no setup
        appears, take nothing — there is no quota and a flat session is not a failure.

  [ADDED]
        NOW: Hold to a structure break, not to a point count: for a long, exit when price
        takes out the low of the pullback you entered from; mirrored for a short. No fixed-
        point profit target. The entire week's profit came from the handful of trades held
        into 26–58% of their swing; the day where every trade was correctly on its swing but
        each was cut small made almost nothing (+$154 on 7 clean trades).

  [ADDED]
        NOW: Mid-session self-check from your own fills: if you have three or more closed
        trades and each captured only a small fraction of the swing it sat on, the fault is
        your exits, not your entries — stop adding trades and hold the next correct entry
        strictly by rule 6.

  [REWRITTEN]
        WAS: Never take a trade against the side you have declared. Against-the-leg trades
        were the single largest identified cost of the week (−$282 and −$1,056 on the two
        days they appeared, including a day that lost over a thousand dollars in two
        trades).
        NOW: Take no trade against the dominant side, ever. Counter-side trades lost money
        on every single day they appeared (−$38, −$792, −$418, −$314), including both
        winning days and the best day of the week. There is no version of this that is worth
        testing again.

  [REWRITTEN]
        WAS: Stop trading for the day when realised P&L reaches a loss of roughly three
        average winning trades, or after three consecutive losses on the declared side.
        Three consecutive losses on one side means the side is wrong and the day is
        unreadable; do not switch sides to make it back.
        NOW: Stop for the session after three losing trades, and never try to recover a
        losing day by taking the other side. The declared side being wrong is a reason to be
        flat, not a reason to flip.

  [REWRITTEN]
        WAS: Flip the side only when a leg against your side exceeds the size of the largest
        leg in your direction so far that day. Nothing smaller changes your side — not a
        pullback, not a long stall, not a round number, not your own losing trade.
        NOW: Change sides only when a counter-swing grows larger than the biggest swing so
        far in your direction. Not a pullback, not a long stall, not a losing trade of your
        own, not a round number, not the clock.

  [REWRITTEN]
        WAS: Decide the day's side from the picture before entering, and define it
        mechanically: if the current price is above the day's opening area and the last
        completed leg was UP, the day's side is long; if below and the last completed leg
        was DOWN, the side is short. Trade only that side until the rule below forces a
        flip.
        NOW: Name the dominant side mechanically from what is already drawn: the direction
        of the largest completed swing of the day so far, with current price on that side of
        the day's opening area. That is the only side you trade until rule 3 forces a
        change.

  [REWRITTEN]
        WAS: Cut immediately — no second chance, no averaging, no widening — if price breaks
        the extreme that defined the setup in rule 4. That break is the only acceptable
        loss; a loss from anything else means a rule was broken.
        NOW: Cut at once, no widening and no averaging, if price erases the extreme that
        created the setup. That is the only loss you are allowed to take; a loss from any
        other cause means a rule was broken, and the next entry waits for a fresh setup.

  (1 rules carried over with the same meaning, reworded)
```
